title: Compatibility inventory & regimen for fallback model variants (tokenizer/context/tooling)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable inventory and maintenance regimen that ensures fallback model variants are compatible across tokenizer behavior, context/KV cache semantics, and tooling (eval harness, rollout gates, SDKs). This ticket defines the automation scope (snapshot + diffing), parity scoring, and follow-up remediation process so smart routing can safely pick fallbacks by region/tier without surprising tokenization or context truncation regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated inventory job that exports tokenizer tokenization examples and context-handling metrics for every variant in the model catalog (hosted + dedicated + private), executed nightly
A compatibility score per variant pair (0-100) based on tokenizer alignment, max-sequence semantics, and KV cache interoperability
A first-pass diff report and triage queue created for any variant pair with score < 85
Integration of the compatibility check into smart-routing canary gating: fallbacks with score < 80 are excluded from auto-fallbacks; warnings surfaced in Console
Documentation page and runbook for on-call remediation and deterministic repro steps (seeded prompts + failing traces)
checklist: Design data model for compatibility snapshots (tokenization samples, seq-len behavior, tooling API contract) - DONE
Implement snapshot exporter that runs against model inference endpoints - IN PROGRESS
Build diff engine to compute tokenizer/token-id mismatches and context-truncation deltas - IN PROGRESS
Define parity scoring heuristics and thresholds in collaboration with Applied ML - TODO

Create remediation runbook + small set of automated fixes (tokenizer shim, context-normalization) - TODO

2026-02-16 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype exporter implemented for hosted models; collects sample tokenizations for a canonical seed set and logs token-id sequences to S3.

2026-02-25 - Applied ML review (Maya Chen): Proposed scoring weight: tokenizer 50%, sequence-truncation 30%, tooling API contract 20%. Need to validate weights against historical regression incidents.
2026-03-03 - Runtime review (Diego Morales): KV cache handshake differences surfaced for two internal variants; added KV-miss trace capture to exporter.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Rina Gupta): Console UI mockups for: pair-list table, score histogram, and quick-repro link. PM asks to surface per-region variant prevalence.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Diff engine MVP generates pair reports and flags 12 pairs with score < 85. Created triage Jira board and initial remediation tickets for top-3 customer-facing models.
comments: Maya Chen (Applied ML) - 2026-02-26: We should add fuzzy tokenizer equivalence tests to tolerate benign byte-level differences introduced by quantization pipelines.
Diego Morales (Runtime) - 2026-03-04: KV cache semantics differ when models change eos-token strategy. Suggest augmenting exporter to include end-of-sequence handling traces.
Rina Gupta (Design) - 2026-03-10: Console needs a triage action that links to automated repro artifacts (seed prompt + trace) to speed up incident response.
Aisha Patel (PM) - 2026-03-11: Prioritize remediation for variants that are present in >5% of regional traffic over a 7-day window.
Security (notes) - 2026-03-12: No customer data is stored in plain text; ensure seed prompt set excludes PII — added to exporter sanitization checklist.
risks: False positives from tokenizer diffs could block valid fallback variants, increasing latency/cost by forcing higher-tier routing.
Nightly snapshot cost on Dedicated/private endpoints could be non-trivial; need to throttle and sample by region/tier.
Automated fixes (shim layers) might mask deeper model incompatibilities and create long-term maintenance burden.
next_steps: Complete diff engine unit tests and run across the full hosted catalog (target 2026-03-18)
Align scoring thresholds with Applied ML after running the scoring model on historical incidents (target 2026-03-20)
Prototype Console integration for gating feedback in the smart-routing UI (design + API contract) - target 2026-03-22
Coordinate with Solutions Eng to run the inventory exporter inside two customer Private deployments to validate non-hosted paths (target 2026-03-25)
notes: We intentionally separate tokenizer checks from context/KV checks to keep the scoring explainable for on-call engineers.
Fallback gating policy proposal: score >= 90 allowed for auto-fallback; 80-89 allowed behind a canary rollout; <80 blocked from auto-fallback and must be manually qualified.
Long-term: consider adding tokenizer normalization as part of model onboarding to reduce drift between variants.
